name: Osaka
tagline: Takoyaki since 1972 in Dotonbori, and the Bib Gourmand okonomiyaki that always has a line.

Honke Ootako.description: Generous octopus balls since 1972, mentioned in the Michelin Guide, right in Dotonbori.

Kiji.description: Okonomiyaki with a constant line in Umeda, recognized with a Bib Gourmand.

Kashiwaya.description: Signature kaiseki in a residential corner of Suita, reviewed by critic Andy Hayler. Three Michelin stars.

Kani Doraku Dotonbori Honten.description: Osaka's most iconic crab restaurant, recognizable by the giant 6-meter mechanical crab on its Dotonbori facade. Anthony Bourdain stopped here on "No Reservations."

Genrokuzushi.description: The spot that invented conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) in 1958, an invention born in Osaka.

Hajime.description: Avant-garde French fine dining by chef Hajime Yoneda in Edobori; reached three Michelin stars in 2009, in record time after opening.

Taian.description: Precise kaiseki by chef Hitoshi Takahata in a discreet Osaka space; has held three Michelin stars since 2011.

Fujiya 1935.description: Signature cuisine blending Japanese technique with Mediterranean influences; chef Tetsuya Fujiwara is the fourth generation of a restaurant family whose first shop opened in 1935.

Koryu.description: Intimate kaiseki in the Kitashinchi district seating only about ten guests; has held Michelin recognition for more than a decade.

Sushi Sanshin.description: An eight-seat sushi counter that makes use of daytime natural light; one Michelin star and several consecutive years of the Gault et Millau prize.

Naniwa Kappo Kigawa.description: Traditional kappo cuisine right in Dotonbori, recognized by the Michelin Guide, where the chef prepares each seasonal dish in front of diners at the counter.

Endo Sushi.description: A century-old sushi shop inside Osaka's former central fish market, famed for its ultra-fresh tuna and red miso clam soup.

Yoshino Zushi.description: Founded in 1841 in the Senba district, this is the house that perfected hako-zushi (box-pressed sushi), a distinctly Osaka style unlike Tokyo-style nigiri.

Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai Sohonten.description: The original 1929 shop in Shinsekai, birthplace of kushikatsu; its mascot with the 'no double-dipping' sign is a neighborhood icon.

Kuromon Ichiba Market.description: Known as 'Osaka's kitchen', this 580-meter covered market traces back to 1822 near Enmyoji temple and today gathers fresh seafood, fugu, and takoyaki and okonomiyaki stalls.

Wanaka.description: One of Osaka's longest-running takoyaki chains, founded in 1952 near Namba; its dashi-heavy batter made it famous across Japan.

Aizuya.description: In the Tamade neighborhood, this shop founded in 1933 is considered the birthplace of takoyaki, created by Tomekichi Endo; it's served without sauce to highlight the octopus flavor.

Kukuru.description: A takoyaki stand in Dotonbori recognizable by its giant octopus sculpture on the facade, one of the neighborhood's most photographed symbols.

Mizuno.description: Okonomiyaki served since 1945 from the same three-story Dotonbori building, rebuilt after the wartime bombings; an unbroken Bib Gourmand since 2016.

Chibo.description: Okonomiyaki spot founded in 1973 occupying an entire building on the Dotonbori canal, the original location behind more than 70 branches across Japan.

Kinryu Ramen.description: Opened in 1982 in Dotonbori, it popularized tonkotsu broth in Osaka; its facade with a giant three-dimensional golden dragon is one of the most photographed spots in the area, and it's open 24 hours.

Kamukura.description: Osaka-born ramen chain with a lighter vegetable-based broth, overseen by a 'soup sommelier' who keeps the flavor consistent across every location.

Dotonbori Imai Honten.description: Udon shop founded in 1946 in a traditional dark-tiled building; its kitsune udon with a golden dashi of Hokkaido kelp and Kyushu mackerel is its signature dish.

Tsuruichi.description: Historic yakiniku in Tsuruhashi, Osaka's Koreatown, with a house sauce that has remained unchanged since the 1940s.

Izakaya Tokitame.description: Neighborhood izakaya near Fukushima Station serving sashimi and locally raised chicken tataki, recognized with the Michelin Guide's Bib Gourmand.

Ajinoya.description: Okonomiyaki spot near Dotonbori serving since 1965, with a Bib Gourmand since the first Kyoto/Osaka guide in 2016; each dish is cooked on the griddle in front of the customer.

Yaekatsu.description: 1949 kushikatsu spot in Shinsekai, the locals' favorite as an alternative to Daruma's lines; its fluffy batter is made with local yam.

Jiyuken.description: Opened in 1910 in Namba, it's considered Osaka's first Western-style (yoshoku) restaurant; its mixed curry topped with a raw egg has stayed the same across four generations.

Arabiya Coffee.description: A traditional Japanese kissaten from 1951 near Hozenji temple, famous for its nel-drip filter coffee and its tamagoyaki omelet sandwich; the original hand-crank roaster is still displayed upstairs.

Bar Nayuta.description: A menu-less speakeasy cocktail bar in Nishishinsaibashi: the bartender crafts a bespoke drink based on the spirit you request. It entered the extended Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 list.

Genpin Hozenji Sohonten.description: A fugu (pufferfish) specialist born in Osaka more than four decades ago, with over 130 licensed chefs across its network; this branch sits beside Hozenji temple.

Ayamuya.description: Osaka's only Michelin-starred yakitori restaurant, on a quiet Fukushima street; the chef adjusts charcoal, salt, and cut for each piece of Tamba Jidori chicken.

Soba Takama.description: Michelin one-star soba at surprisingly affordable prices, a short walk from Tenjinbashisuji Rokuchome Station; open for only a few hours at lunchtime.

Ayamedo.description: A soba specialist housed in a former Showa-era merchant house, holding a Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand.

Tonkatsu Fujii.description: A seven-seat counter in Asahi-ku where the tonkatsu is prepared in full view of the guest; online reservations only, no calls or walk-ins accepted. A Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand.

Kura Sushi Nakamozu.description: This Nakamozu, Sakai location opened in 1984 as the first conveyor-belt sushi restaurant of the Kura Sushi chain, founded in Osaka in 1977 and now spread across half the world.

Chukasoba Mugen.description: House-broth ramen in Fukushima-ku, with seven consecutive Bib Gourmand awards and recurring placement in Japan's Top 100 Ramen ranking.

Rikuro Ojisan no Mise.description: A Namba shop opened in 1957 that reinvented Japanese cheesecake in 1984: fluffy, jiggly, and stamped with 'Uncle Rikuro's' face on the box; it went viral on social media for its lines and texture.

Temmabashi Fujikawa.description: Tempura with one Michelin star for six consecutive years beside the Okawa river; it uses cottonseed oil and an egg-free batter, characteristic of the Osaka style.

Tsuruhashi Fugetsu Honten.description: Born in postwar Tsuruhashi, it popularized modanyaki (okonomiyaki topped with noodles) and pioneered adding kimchi to the mix; it now has more than sixty locations across the Kansai region.
